transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I suppose… what finally made me say something is after I eat too much, I’ve been going upstairs and making myself throw up. And then I come back down and act like I’ve just been tidying the kitchen, or getting ready for bed.

It sounds ridiculous when I say it out loud. I’m an optician, so I’m used to noticing tiny details all day, frames sitting unevenly, that sort of thing, and yet at home I’ve got this whole routine I’m pretending isn’t happening. It’s been hard to admit.
Do you find yourself particularly concerned about your body shape or weight, or has avoiding gaining weight become a major focus for you?

Yes… yes, it has, though I feel silly admitting it at my age. My daughter’s said I look too thin, and there’s a woman at church who mentioned it too—she’s one of those people who notices everything, always arranging the flowers just so—but even with that, if my skirt feels a bit tight, or the scale is up even one pound, I panic. It’s like I’ve suddenly become huge overnight, even though part of me knows that can’t be true.
Do you ever feel like you lose control over how much you're eating, like you can't stop eating once you start, or that you're eating large amounts of food in a short period of time?

Yes… that’s exactly it, really. Once I start, it’s like a switch flips, and I can almost hear myself saying, “Linda, stop now, that’s enough,” but I don’t. My hands just keep going back for more, almost like I’m watching someone else do it.

It’s strange, because at work I’m so controlled—measuring, adjusting frames, making sure everything’s precise—and then at home it’s the complete opposite. I don’t feel in charge of it once it starts.
Do you often make yourself vomit after eating to try to prevent gaining weight?

Yes… I do. Not every single time I eat, but after I’ve eaten too much, that’s what I’ve been doing.

I go upstairs and make myself throw up, and then I come back down and pretend I was just tidying the kitchen or getting ready for bed. It’s awful, really, because I’ll even think about how long I’ve been gone, whether anyone’s noticed… like when I’m at work and I’m watching all the little details, except this time I’m trying to hide them.

And yes, it is because I’m frightened of gaining weight.
